title: 2Klips Dating App Infrastructure
summary: Planned and migrated a projected 500K-user social application topology to AWS arrays.
description: Architected and executed a full cloud migration for a social dating platform targeting 500K+ concurrent users. Designed a multi-AZ VPC topology with public/private subnet segmentation, NAT gateways, and ALB-based ingress routing. Provisioned EKS clusters with auto-scaling node groups via Terraform, and implemented zero-downtime blue/green deployments through GitHub Actions CI/CD pipelines. Set up RDS Aurora with automated failover, S3-backed media storage with CloudFront CDN distribution, and IAM roles with least-privilege access policies across all service accounts.
highlights: Reduced infrastructure provisioning time from days to ~12 minutes via Terraform modules
Achieved 99.95% uptime SLA through multi-AZ deployment and automated failover
Cut deployment pipeline runtime by 40% with parallelized GitHub Actions workflows
Implemented cost-tagging strategy, reducing monthly AWS spend by ~22%

title: Centralized K8s Management Engine
summary: FastAPI multi-cluster dashboard for tracking real-time node scaling alerts and pod workload metrics.
description: Built an internal operational dashboard using FastAPI and the Kubernetes Python client to provide unified visibility across multiple clusters. The platform aggregates node health, pod status, resource utilization, and HPA scaling events into a single pane. Custom alerting rules push notifications via webhook when node CPU/memory thresholds are breached. Prometheus metrics are scraped and surfaced alongside deployment history, making it trivial to correlate incidents with recent rollouts.
highlights: Unified observability across multiple independent Kubernetes clusters from a single UI
Automated node-scaling event logging, reducing on-call incident response time by 35%
Integrated Prometheus alertmanager webhooks for real-time Slack notifications
Containerized and deployed via Helm chart with configurable cluster endpoints

title: Automated Ubuntu CIS Hardening Framework
summary: Automated repeatable OS hardening profiles presented on stage at UbuCon Asia 2025.
description: Developed a fully automated CIS hardening framework for Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 servers using Ansible playbooks. The solution covers kernel parameter tuning, service disabling, filesystem mount hardening, PAM configuration, auditd rules, and SSH lockdown. Wazuh SIEM agents are deployed alongside for continuous compliance monitoring and drift detection. The framework was battle-tested on bare-metal and VM environments before being presented live on stage at UbuCon Asia 2025 in Kathmandu.
highlights: Presented the automated hardening framework at UbuCon Asia 2025, Kathmandu
Automated 200+ CIS benchmark controls across Ubuntu LTS releases
Reduced manual hardening time from ~6 hours per server to under 8 minutes
Presented and demonstrated live at UbuCon Asia 2025, Kathmandu
Integrated Wazuh for post-hardening continuous compliance scoring

title: Sabai / Dammi Platform Pipelines
summary: Deployment pipelines and multi-environment orchestration for container integrity checks.
description: Designed and implemented end-to-end CI/CD pipelines for Sabai / Dammi project. Pipelines handle Docker image builds with layer caching, Trivy vulnerability scanning as a pipeline gate, multi-environment promotion (dev → staging → production), and Nginx reverse-proxy configuration management. Jenkins DSL pipelines are version-controlled and parameterized for environment-specific overrides, enabling the development team to ship confidently without manual ops intervention.
highlights: Implemented Trivy as a hard pipeline gate, blocking builds with CRITICAL CVEs
Built parameterized Jenkins DSL shared library reused across 3 product pipelines
Reduced average deployment cycle from 45 minutes to under 10 minutes
Multi-environment promotion flow with manual approval gates before production

title: tshoot — Linux Infrastructure TUI
summary: Zero-dependency Go TUI for instant Linux server diagnostics — CPU, memory, disk, ports, containers and network in one dashboard.
description: tshoot is a lightweight terminal user interface built natively in Go for accelerating the initial discovery phase of infrastructure incident response. Instead of manually chaining top, df -h, ss -tulpn, ping, and docker logs one by one, tshoot integrates all essential first-step diagnostic vectors into a single real-time dashboard. It communicates directly with the Linux kernel's /proc filesystem rather than scraping shell utility output, keeping its footprint minimal even on resource-exhausted servers. Distributed as a single statically linked binary with zero runtime dependencies.
highlights: Reads CPU, memory, and disk metrics directly from /proc — no shell utility dependencies
Monitors Docker container statuses and streams logs via the Docker daemon API
Real-time port mapping cross-referencing open sockets to owning PIDs
Configurable ping engine for tracking latency to custom infrastructure endpoints
Single statically linked binary — runs on any Linux host with zero install requirements
F4 maximize mode for full-screen panel inspection during active incidents

title: Squeeze — Client-Side Image Compressor
summary: Privacy-first browser-based image compressor and format converter — files never leave the device.
description: Squeeze is a minimalist, privacy-first web application that compresses and converts images entirely within the browser using the HTML5 Canvas API. Built to solve a real problem: submitting sensitive documents (IDs, passports, certificates) to government or institutional portals with strict file size limits, without the privacy risk of uploading them to unknown third-party servers. Zero external framework dependencies — just vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Can be used fully offline after the first load.
highlights: 100% client-side processing — sensitive files never transmitted to any server
Supports JPEG, PNG, and WebP conversion entirely within the browser sandbox
Bulk queue management with per-file settings and side-by-side size previews
Works fully offline after initial page load via browser cache
Zero heavy framework dependencies — entire app is auditable vanilla JS
